      <description>Nødetatene har fått melding om en skolebuss som har kjørt av veien i Larvik.
– Bussen har sklidd av veien og ut i grøfta med alle fire hjul. I bussen er det 24 barn som fremstår uskadd, skriver operasjonsleder Per Magne Eftang i politiloggen.
Bussjåføren er også uskadd, ifølge politiet.
– Barna er nå på vei ut av bussen og inn et hus for å holde varmen, sier Eftang til NRK.
Han sier alle barna brukte bilbelte.
Operasjonslederen antar at hendelsen kan knyttes til det glatte føret, men politiet har ikke kommet fram til stedet ennå.
Klokka 09.44 opplyser politiet at ingen er skadet. Flere foreldre har hentet barna sine og ny buss er klar til å frakte resten av barna til skolen.</description>

    <item>
      <title>CNN: Demokratene vinner historisk senatsvalg i Mississippi</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/cnn_-demokratene-vinner-historisk-senatsvalg-i-mississippi-1.18079865</link>
      <description>Demokraten Scott Colom har vunnet senatsvalget i den tradisjonelt republikanske delstaten Mississippi, ifølge CNNs prognose.
Colom slår dermed den sittende republikanske senatoren Cindy Hyde-Smith, melder CNN onsdag kveld.
Han blir den første demokraten som representerer Mississippi i Senatet på over 40 år.
Colom blir også den første svarte politikeren som velges til et politisk verv av velgerne i hele Mississippi siden gjenoppbyggingsperioden etter den amerikanske borgerkrigen på 1800-tallet.
Valget ble holdt 3. november, men opptellingen har trukket ut i over en uke. Onsdag ettermiddag ledet Colom med rundt 3000 stemmer da om lag 98 prosent av stemmene var talt opp.
Resultatet er ennå ikke formelt godkjent. Fylkene i delstaten har frist til fredag med å godkjenne sine valgresultater.
(NTB)</description>

      <description>Det føderale politiet FBI etterforsker Nvidia-sjef Jensen Huangs forhold til en kvinne som mistenkes for å ha spionert for Kina, sa president Donald Trump under en pressebriefing mandag kveld.
Trump sa også at Huang «ikke ante» at kvinnen angivelig er en kinesisk spion.
– Jeg stilte ham spørsmålet: 'Hadde du noen anelse om at hun var spion?' Han svarte: 'Jeg ante overhodet ikke at hun var spion,' og jeg tror ham virkelig, sa Trump.
Avsløringen av den 63 år gamle Nvidia-sjefens utenomekteskapelige forhold har rystet børsene, det politiske miljøet og teknologibransjen i USA.</description>

      <description>Republikaneren Thomas Massie har levert et riksrettsforslag mot forsvarsminister Pete Hegseth i Representantenes hus.

      <description>– Det vil bli opprettet en straffesak, sier politiadvokat Erlend Bakke til NRK.
Han er mistenkt for kroppskrenkelse og uberettiget adgang, sier han. Den mistenkte har ikke fått oppnevnt noen forsvarer i saken.

– Det vil bli gjennomført avhør med partene, sier Bakke til NRK.

Han ønsker ikke å gå nærmere inn på hvilke etterforskningsskritt som har blitt gjort eller som skal gjennomføres.
Det var natt til fredag at en mann trengte seg inn i hjemmet til Marius Borg Høiby på Skaugum og dyttet ham.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Kongen fullførte maraton på tiden 4.43.01</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/kongen-fullforte-maraton-pa-tiden-4.43.01-1.18076803</link>
      <description>Kongen og kronprinsessen er deltakere i French Riviera Marathon, i Nice sør i Frankrike.
Kong Haakon løp i mål på tiden 4.43.01, ifølge sporingstjenesten Trackanza.
Det var TV 2 som meldte saken først.
Et bilde viser kongen og kronprinsessen løpende ved siden av hverandre under maratonet. I maratonet er kronprinsessen registrert som Ingrid Alexandra og kongen som Haakon Magnus.
Startskuddet gikk klokka 09.16, og distansen er helmaraton på 42,125 kilometer. Løypen går langs den franske rivieraen fra Nice til Cannes.
Lørdag formiddag opplyste Slottet på nettsidene sine at «statsrådet forestår bestyrelsen av riket».
Ifølge nettsidene var kongen og kronprinsessen på privat opphold i utlandet. Det betyr at regjeringen har ansvaret for å styre og forvalte landet.
(NTB/NRK)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Ny norsk gulltriumf i VM i skyting</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/ny-norsk-gulltriumf-i-vm-i-skyting-1.18076796</link>
      <description>Caroline Finnestad Lund, Jeanette Hegg Duestad og Synnøve Berg tok laggullet på 50 meter rifle match i VM i skyting i Doha søndag.
Det var Lunds andre gull i mesterskapet. Lørdag ble 21-åringen verdensmester på 50 meter 60 skudd liggende.
Norge sanket totalt 1764 poeng under lagkonkurransen, og de kom 3,0 poeng foran Sveits på 2.-plass. Tsjekkia stakk av med bronsemedaljen. De var to poeng bak sveitserne igjen.
I eliminasjonen for lag 1 ble Finnestad Lund nummer fire med 588 poeng. Synnøve Berg ble nummer sju med 586 poeng. Duestad ble nummer tre med 590 poeng i lag 2.
Alle de tre norske jentene er videre til kvalifiseringen i den individuelle konkurransen i den samme øvelsen mandag. (NTB)</description>

   <description>Nach einem Treffen mit dem Kremlchef zeigt sich US-Unterhändler Kushner vorsichtig optimistisch. Zwar gibt es weiter große Differenzen zwischen Moskau und Kyjiw, doch auch ein großer Gefangenenaustausch zeichnet sich ab.</description>

Neighbours of a shipbreaking facility in Union Bay are worried the company is planning to bring another barge. The province cancelled the company’s former foreshore lease in 2025, and neighbours want to make sure they follow the rules.

People living near the Deep Water Recovery (DWR) site were glad to see a RCMP boat Thursday.

There were at least two pieces of equipment running at the facility and neighbours said the company appears to be preparing to pull the barge onshore.

“Probably over a week that they’ve been inching it up and now they have it on some rollers but it’s trespassing as far as the Ministry of Environment says so we’re wondering why we’re not seeing any action around here,” said Kathy Calder, a concerned neighbour.

Calder says she’s among the neighbours who have reported what’s been happening to the federal and provincial governments, as it falls under the jurisdiction of both.

DWR has wanted to operate a ship recycling facility at the site for years but it’s never had the community, regional district or first nations approval.

A neighbour often documents what’s happening at the site with a drone.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

B.C.’s Ministry of Environment still can’t say much while the provincial government transitions, but notes that in July 2025, the Ministry of Water, Land and Resource Stewardship cancelled DWR’s former foreshore lease after they failed to provide additional financial security and due to repeated non-compliances identified by the ministry.

The Natural Resource Officer Service (NROS) has issued a Land Act trespass notice to address the unauthorized use of Crown land.

The government says it’s continuing to investigate.

“If the lease is pulled there should be no movement down there and this is about the fifth time we’ve seen trespassing go on,” said Calder.

Neighbours did notice something unusual Thursday, something Calder says is a first. The RCMP’s MV Inkster pulled up near shore.

“For 15 minutes they actually looked like they were quite close to shore, maybe taking pictures or talking to the owner or CAO down there on the shore,” said Calder.

Neighbours hope it’s a sign of government investigation.

In a statement, Josie Osborne, the MLA-elect for the region thanks the neighbours for their ongoing vigilance and for reporting activities to her office, to provincial officials, and to the RAPP line.

She says “for the past six years, she’s been actively pushing for stronger oversight and enforcement of Deep Water Recovery’s operations.”

“I personally feel ripped off because this is costing an awful lot of money,” said Calder.

CHEK News reached out to both the RCMP the Deep Water Recovery but did not receive a response by deadline.

Vancouver Island is prone to wild weather but the extremes are becoming more frequent. From record-breaking heat and wildfire threats to powerful storms and flooding, scientists warn that as the planet warms, the risks to our communities will only grow.  

On June 29, 2021, a heat dome settled over the province and the temperature in Lytton reached an extreme 49 degrees Celsius, the hottest ever recorded across B.C.

The next day, a devastating wildfire ripped through the town, destroying 90 per cent of all structures.

Five months later, a series of powerful atmospheric rivers unleashed record rainfall across B.C. and Vancouver Island, triggering catastrophic flooding, landslides and widespread destruction.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

Andrew Weaver, Professor Emeritus, School of Earth and Ocean Sciences University of Victoria said the weather is venturing into uncharted territory.

“We’ve got to start getting used to this. We are going to get much much warmer, and these El Niños are going to get much much stronger. And precipitation is going to get much, much bigger. And the climate is changing at a rate that is unparalleled in several million years. So it’s not a good situation,” Weaver said.

Atmospheric rivers have become part of B.C.’s weather system.

Charles Curry, climate scientist for Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium (PCIC) at the University of Victoria (UVic) said studies indicate the intensity of atmospheric rivers, and the amount of moisture they carry, is growing.

“The majority have found that the intensities, or the amount of rainfall that will come in any given atmospheric river by about mid-century, and then into the late century is projected to be larger than it has been in the past. So that’s an individual storm,” Curry said.

The BC Coroners Service found 619 people died as a direct result of the heat dome in 2021.
At least five people died as a direct result of flooding, and mudslides during 2021’s atmospheric rivers.

READ RELATED: B.C. government marks 5 years since heat dome killed hundreds

Two people died on Vancouver Island during the October 2024 atmospheric river when their vehicles were swept off the washed-out Bamfield Road.

“Interior BC wildfires are out of control. They are going to get far worse. The boreal forest is already slumping because of permafrost degradation, and beetle infestation. And there’s going to be wildfires in the boreal forest,” Weaver said.

Scientists agree that if global temperatures rise by two degrees Celsius by the end of the century, extreme weather events will become more frequent and intense.

The Supreme Court of Canada won’t hear an appeal challenging the application of British Columbia’s foreign buyer tax on a real estate purchase involving joint ownership by a Canadian citizen and a foreign national.

The B.C. Court of Appeal had previously dismissed an appeal brought by a couple who jointly bought an apartment in Richmond, B.C., putting 95 per cent in the Canadian woman’s name, and five per cent in the name of her foreign partner.

But the man had actually paid 40 per cent of the purchase price, with the woman explaining the disparity by saying it was a Chinese custom for a husband to pay a “bride price” by buying his wife a home. 

The couple, who were engaged in 2014 when they bought the home under a presale contract, paid the foreign buyer tax on only the five per cent registered to the foreign man, but an audit later found the tax “payable on the fair market value of the whole property.”

The B.C. government had told the lower court the rule was meant to “prevent tax avoidance by foreign investors who own beneficial interests held indirectly by others.”

The Supreme Court of Canada refused the couple leave to appeal on Thursday.

The couple had claimed imposing the tax on the entire value of the property was “profoundly unfair,” but the three-judge panel of the Appeal Court found they could have avoided paying the tax on the property’s entire value if they had registered ownership based on their contributions to the purchase price. 

The appellate ruling from earlier this year said the man, Li-Yuan Chuang, paid 40 per cent of the purchase price, but registered only a five per cent stake in the property, which the couple declared to have a value of $474,500 at the time of purchase.

His Canadian partner, Chia-Wen Hsia, said it was “customary in Chinese culture to pay for ‘bride price’ as in the husband buying a house for the wife.”

“In my husband’s case, he is not rich so he could only pay for part of the purchase price,” Hsia is quoted as saying in the appellate ruling. 

The B.C. Supreme Court initially dismissed the couple’s legal challenge in 2024.

The most recent assessed value for the two-bedroom apartment in the Avanti Richmond complex is $820,000.

The original B.C. Supreme Court ruling said a B.C. Finance Ministry tax analyst put the additional tax owed by the couple at just over $126,000. 

The B.C. foreign buyer tax is 20 per cent of market value.

The couple’s lawyer, Massao Morinaga, said they had no comment about the Supreme Court of Canada’s dismissal of the case.

He said it was the “end of the road judicially,” but the current foreign buyer tax legislation is drafted in a way that “captures situations that are inequitable.”

]]> 1360976 Despite recent rain, 2 wildfires continue to burn on Vancouver Island https://cheknews.ca/despite-recent-rain-2-wildfires-continue-to-burn-on-vancouver-island-1360948/ Thu, 12 Nov 2026 22:44:25 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1360948

The wildfire season is no longer top of mind for most British Columbians, especially as the winter storms have arrived, but two wildfires continue to burn on Southern Vancouver Island.

The post Despite recent rain, 2 wildfires continue to burn on Vancouver Island appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The wildfire season is no longer top of mind for most British Columbians, especially as the winter storms have arrived, but two wildfires continue to burn on Southern Vancouver Island.

The Mount Jack wildfire, just north of Sooke, has remained active since Sept. 20, though it is now under control. It’s listed at 337.23 hectares in size as of Thursday.

Another wildfire northwest of the Mount Jack wildfire was discovered on Nov. 3, but it remains listed as being held. It is near Clapp Creek with a size of 0.009 hectares.

Erika Berg, fire information officer with BC Wildfire Service, says there is good containment on the fires, but they do remain active.

“We’re not anticipating them necessarily growing,” Berg said to CHEK News.

“However, there is likely still activity within the perimeter and burning deeper.”

Burning deeper means that there is dry fuel deep in the ground, sometimes into the root systems of trees.

“Even though it maybe doesn’t look like it from just a glance, there can be activity burning beneath the surface, and so in the stages of mop up and patrol, that is some rigorous work where we have crews on the ground digging and flipping soil over to identify and extinguish any remaining hotspots,” she said.

“So it’s a long process, and it can certainly take some time, especially when there are some inaccessible areas that we can’t actually get on the ground to see.”

The Mount Jack wildfire in particular is still burning in inaccessible areas.

“So we are requiring our indices to reach certain levels before we can feel confident to call these fully extinguished,” Berg said.

Berg says wildfires are unpredictable, so it’s difficult to say exactly what conditions are needed in order for these two fires to finally be extinguished.

“There is the potential if we keep trending towards cool and wet that it may reach those deeper layers and help with eventual extinguishment,” Berg said.

“It is a waiting game, unfortunately. But no risk to public safety. The containment has been established. It’s just a matter of waiting for us to be able to confidently consider it extinguished.”

For now, the two wildfires aren’t constantly being staffed by BC Wildfire crews.

“It’s more so letting Mother Nature run its course and then strategically timing people to go in, give it a look, do some more patrol, and because it can be a large area too, it takes time to be able to confidently call it out.”

Across the province, there are still 23 active wildfires, four are being held with the remaining all under control.

]]> 1360948 Carney in Ireland for meetings with European leaders ahead of Asia summits https://cheknews.ca/carney-in-ireland-for-meetings-with-european-leaders-ahead-of-asia-summits-1360961/ Thu, 12 Nov 2026 22:32:22 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1360961

Prime Minister Mark Carney continued his push for closer economic and security ties between Canada and Europe at a political summit in Ireland on Thursday.

The post Carney in Ireland for meetings with European leaders ahead of Asia summits appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Prime Minister Mark Carney continued his push for closer economic and security ties between Canada and Europe at a political summit in Ireland on Thursday.

The prime minister also met with the leaders of two of the nine European nations that have yet to ratify a decade-old trade deal.

Carney was in Dublin for a meeting of the European Political Community, an informal gathering of leaders from around Europe that has occurred every six months since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

On the sidelines, he sat down with both Cyprus President Nikos Christodoulides and Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis to discuss negotiations to strengthen Canadian-European ties.

Greece and Cyprus have not yet ratified the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement. Christodoulides indicated that could soon change, at least for his nation.

“I want to mention this publicly. We are doing whatever is necessary in order to pass the agreement, (the) free trade agreement between the European Union and Canada, which is very important for both of us,” he said during a photo op ahead of his private conversation with Carney.

Both countries have held back for reasons that include questions about protected origins for cheeses — such as whether Canadian-made products can be called feta or halloumi.

Christodoulides said the meeting was the first between a Canadian prime minister and a Cypriot president in 80 years. He said it reflects the “pro-European Canadian approach” under Carney’s leadership.

Carney also had informal discussions, known as pull-asides, with French President Emmanuel Macron and the leaders of Latvia, Ireland and Denmark. France and Ireland also have not ratified CETA, which effectively has been in place since 2017.

Carney’s trip to Dublin marks the second time Canada has been invited to the European Political Community meeting. And for the second time, Canada was the only non-European country represented at the table.

Since the last meeting in May in Armenia, Carney and European Union leaders have pitched making Canada an “associate member” of the EU — a title they have yet to define.

Carney told reporters Thursday morning that the summit could help advance his goal of boosting affordability and economic opportunities for Canadians through new partnerships with Europe.

“It delivers opportunity — opportunity for our youth, for our artists, for companies. It will deliver affordability, cutting red tape, more competition in Canada, more goods, more choice and security,” he said in English.

Thursday’s summit included Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who briefed Carney and a dozen European leaders on the state of negotiations with Russia.

The Ukrainian leader discussed this week’s talks in Abu Dhabi with Russian officials organized by U.S. President Donald Trump’s envoy Steve Witkoff and his son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Zelenskyy had not presented a public summary of those talks by Thursday evening. His briefing took place as Witkoff and Kushner were in Moscow to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Witkoff and Kushner are expected to fly to Dublin to meet with Zelenskyy.

Carney said it’s up to Europe to craft arrangements that will secure an eventual peace, with support from countries like Canada.

These “security guarantees” can include promises to provide troops to ensure a ceasefire holds, or to defend a country if it is invaded.

“Security guarantees are a European responsibility, with Canada, with the United States. So there are tiers for security guarantees,” Carney said in French.

The Associated Press reports that NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said Thursday that the U.S., Europe and Ukraine are “very much aligned” on what the security guarantees should look like once a viable peace is established.

The United Kingdom has convened Canada, Australia, Japan and numerous EU countries in what it calls a coalition of the willing aimed at providing military support to Ukraine once a ceasefire is in place.

Carney spoke briefly with reporters at the start of Thursday’s meetings, but most of the plenary was not broadcast. He is expected to give a press conference in coming days.

The summit’s Irish hosts have locked down a section of central Dublin for what they are calling its largest ever gathering of international leaders. Police boats have been patrolling the River Liffey and there is a visible security presence across the city.

Schools, newsrooms and an airline have reported receiving bomb threats which local authorities have said are not credible.

Carney is set to leave for Asia Thursday evening.

He will attend a summit in the Philippines focused on regional issues, followed by the Francophonie summit in Cambodia.

The Francophonie summit will also include Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, whose minority government was elected on a sovereigntist platform.

Plamondon has said he wants to conduct diplomacy on Quebec’s behalf instead of leaving it to the prime minister.

On the sidelines of Thursday’s meeting, Macron said he looks forward to speaking with all representatives to the Francophonie at the upcoming summit.

“It is not my place to interfere in Canadian affairs, but rather to continue supporting our shared affinities, including our cultural and linguistic ties,” he said in French.

Carney said he did not attend this week’s UN Climate Conference in Turkey — better known as COP31 — because the leaders’ day fell on Nov. 11.

“It was more important to be at Remembrance Day to honour the women and men of the Canadian Forces who served our country, who stood for democracy, often in Europe, [and] supported our rights,” he said.

Carney added that his environment minister will help advance Canadian interests on electrification, saying it’s a major theme of the summit in Turkey.

Fisheries and Oceans Canada says a landowner in B.C. is out more than $150,000 after they were ordered to restore a damaged fish habitat under the federal Fisheries Act.

The landowner was ordered to pay for repairs under section 38(7.1) of the Fisheries Act after a contractor dug up fish habitat along Toboggan Creek near Smithers between Oct. 3 and Oct. 13, 2023, during what the DFO calls a “peak period for salmon migration and spawning.”

The DFO says the landowner was not charged under the Fisheries Act since they cooperated through the investigation and paid approximately $155,000 for restoration work to the fish habitat.

The DFO describes Toboggan Creek as a “high value system” that’s used by coho salmon, pink salmon, rainbow trout, bull trout, steelhead, and other aquatic species.

“The Court found that digging up the creek bed, filling in the creek channel and removing vegetation along the banks damaged and destroyed fish habitat,” said Fisheries and Oceans Canada on Nov. 6.

“The work was carried out without the authorizations required under the Fisheries Act and the Water Sustainability Act.”

The DFO says it has resources on its website for people who are planning projects near water.

It also asks anyone who spots a suspected fisheries violation to contact the DFO Pacific Region at 1-800-465-4336, or email DFO.ORR-ONS.MPO@dfo-mpo.gc.ca.

CHICAGO (AP) — A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday, with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant’s suite of apps.

Nearly 130,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook just after 1 p.m. ET. New reports have since fallen from that peak, but many said they couldn’t send and receive emails, or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether.

Thousands also reported issues with Microsoft’s workplace messaging app Teams, as well as its AI assistant Copilot and wider Microsoft 365 services.

Microsoft said that it was investigating disruptions, notably related to its email and Teams applications.

In updates posted on social media, Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft said it was aware of users “experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas.”

Microsoft later explained that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” The company determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks.

Microsoft did not immediately provide more information around what might be causing that failure, but added that it was testing a fix.

“We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” the Microsoft 365 Status account wrote on X.

Earlier in the day, the company said it had “successfully restored” problems related to Microsoft Teams in North America, although some users continued to report connectivity issues.
